Published: Oct 15 2025Last updated: Nov 10 2025

- tsunagu Japan
- Kim S.

In this article, we’ll present the latest forecasts for both the autumn foliage and yellow foliage in Japan for 2025. We hope that this guide and the accompanying pictures will help plan your autumn foliage viewing excursions!

## 2025 Autumn Foliage Forecast: Later Than Usual

The activity of viewing and appreciating the changing leaves is essentially the autumn equivalent of springtime [cherry blossom-viewing](https://www.tsunagujapan.com/day-night-hanami-annual-cherry-blossom-viewings-in-japan/), and is known as “momijigari” in Japanese. With the popularity of taking in the beauty of the stunning autumn foliage, predictions for the peak viewing periods across Japan are released every year to help people schedule their foliage-viewing excursions. This article will reference the [Japan Meteorological Agency’s projected dates](https://n-kishou.com/corp/news-contents/autumn/?lang=en), which take temperature and past research into consideration. However, as this is a forecast, the actual peak viewing periods may differ from the posted dates.

Hokkaido is projected to have its leaves change the earliest this year, with the foliage across the country turning subsequently. As this year has seen higher temperatures than normal, the overall turning period is later than usual, stretching into early December across most of Japan.

## What Is the Difference Between the “Autumn Foliage” and “Yellow Foliage”?

To put it simply, “autumn foliage” (“momiji” or “koyo” in Japanese) usually refers to the iconic vibrant red and orange leaves that are often featured in most stunning photos of Japan’s autumn leaves. “Momiji” is also the Japanese term for “maple,” the leaves of which usually turn bright red in the autumn.

Meanwhile, “yellow foliage” (also “koyo” in Japanese), is what the name suggests: leaves that turn yellow in the autumn. This often refers to gingko leaves, which turn a beautiful golden hue.

## Don't Miss Out on Japan's Autumn Views

The peak viewing periods for autumn foliage generally last for around 1 to 2 weeks, although this can change depending on the area and the weather. As a beloved symbol of autumn in Japan, these vibrant leaves attract people from not only across Japan, but also from around the world who want to take in the breathtaking beauty of this striking spectacle. We hope that this list helps you find the spot you want to visit for your own momijigari!

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-13.jpg)

Senjogahara Marshland

Following on with our [2025 autumn reports](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/), today I was happy to visit my favorite autumn spot, [Nikko](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3800.html) in [Tochigi Prefecture](https://www.japan-guide.com/list/e1210.html)!

Although I visited at almost the exact same date as Charly did [last year](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo24/241018_nikko.html), the state seems a little further along in places this time. Many of the spots I visited at higher elevation were already at their best viewing or nearing it, while only the comparatively lower elevation spot of Shoyoen Garden was yet to reach its most vibrant [autumn colors](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2014.html).

This time, I wasn't able to visit some of the mid-elevation spots such as [Irohazaka](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3816.html), [Lake Chuzenjiko](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3806.html) and [Kegon Falls](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3812.html). Given that the lower-elevation spot was so far behind, it is likely that those will continue to be colorful for a few weeks, and overall there will likely be nice spots for viewing until mid November. Higher spots like Ryuzu Falls should remain nice for about a week, mid-elevation spots like the Chuzenjiko area for the rest of the month, while peak colors in the town area will not likely start before early November.

## [Ryuzu Waterfall](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3813.html)

Peak Color

·October 20, 2025

My first spot of the day was the mighty [Ryuzu Waterfall](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3813.html). Although I had driven through rain and fog to get to Nikko, once I got to an altitude of about 1000 meters I found blue skies and blindingly bright sun. I was also happy to find that the [autumn colors](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2014.html) were looking vibrant at the base of the waterfall, with fiery reds and oranges. At the top of the waterfall, there were some rusty browns, but there is still some potential for more color over the coming days.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-01.jpg)

Peak colors at the base of the Ryuzu Waterfall

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-02.jpg)

Beautiful orange leaves by the rushing water

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-03.jpg)

Some vibrant colors on the pathway at the base

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-04.jpg)

More fallen leaves towards the top

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-05.jpg)

Peak colors at the top of the Ryuzu Waterfall

## [Yumoto Onsen](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3807.html)

Peak Color

·October 20, 2025

Next I headed to the small hot spring town of [Yumoto Onsen](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3807.html) to see its lovely Yunoko Lake. Being a bit higher in elevation, at 1478 meters, it was not so surprising to see that the leaves were already fading to brown and some falling, particularly those covering Mount Toyama. Looking towards the east from the northern shore I could see a lot of pretty yellows painting the landscape, though.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-07.jpg)

The mountain was mostly a light brown

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-06.jpg)

There were a few select vibrant trees

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-08.jpg)

Some nice yellows towards the east of the lake

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-09.jpg)

A few nice red trees on the north shore of the lake

## [Senjogahara Marshland](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3811.html)

Approaching Peak

·October 20, 2025

I then started heading to lower elevations, stopping at [Senjogahara Marshland](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3811.html). This spot is popular for its reddish yellow grass and bright yellow larches. While both were visible, overall the landscape felt a little before its best viewing, as there were not many reds and oranges complementing the yellows.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-10.jpg)

The grass had already become a rusty brown, but yellows were still visible

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-11.jpg)

Trees that would have been red around the yellow patches have already lost their leaves

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-12.jpg)

The larches are still yellow, with even some green in places, while others had started losing some leaves

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-13.jpg)

The landscape was still rather lovely in the sun

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-14.jpg)

The little pathway was mostly bare

## [Shoyoen Garden](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3803.html)

Starting to Change

·October 20, 2025

Finally, I headed down towards Nikko's town center to see the [landscape garden](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2099.html) of [Rinnoji Temple](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3803.html), called Shoyoen Garden. I think this was my favorite spot of the day, as it was a very peaceful walk among some vibrant maple leaves. This spot was the least far along in terms of colors, as there were still large patches of green in the trees. The color contrast of greens, reds and oranges made for some nice shots.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-15.jpg)

Beautiful oranges and greens

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-17.jpg)

Only a sprinkling of orange and red here, most of the maples in the shot are still green

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-18.jpg)

A stunning combination of green, red and orange

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-19.jpg)

This part towards the end of the route was so tranquil

And two bonus blooper photos for anyone who got to the end of this report: I also visited [Kegon Waterfall](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3812.html) to see how the leaves were doing there, but was instead greeted by a very thick fog! Such is the fickle nature of Nikko.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-22.jpg)

The waterfall is behind all this fog!

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/g/251020_nikko-23.jpg)

The square by the observation deck was very atmospheric

# Autumn Leaves Forecast 2025

Discover Japan during the beautiful season of autumn leaves
Toyama

Surrounded by rich nature, Japan has four magical seasons. Autumn is considered one of the most beautiful as the landscape turns vibrant shades of orange, yellow, and red. Colorful autumn leaves, known as koyo, have been admired in Japan for centuries and today, together with the Sakura (cherry blossoms), attract a large number of visitors, both local and international. The perfect time to visit these incredible sights is from late September to early December, depending on the place, elevation, and temperature of the year

Each year, the season of scenic autumn leaves begins in colder areas of northern Hokkaido and gradually moves southward to central and southern Japan. In each region, the mountains are colored first, then scenes of colored leaves spread into city gardens, parks, and temples. Both areas are definitely worth a visit.

The secret behind the picturesque vivid foliage lies in Japan’s typical autumn weather – a difference in temperature between cooler mornings, warm sunny daytime, and cold evenings that allow autumn leaves to change.

The scenic autumn season is the time of year when it is neither too hot nor too cold, making it easy and comfortable to travel. This is also the season of harvest and fine seasonal food, which potentially makes autumn the best time for you to visit.

## Guide

November 14, 2025 update

# Introduction to Autumn Colours 2025 in Tohoku Region’s Onsen Resorts – with information about the best time to view fall foliage in different regions

[Guide Tohoku Region](https://selected-ryokan.com/guide/guide-cat/ad-tohoku-region)

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-18_Mt-Kurikoma.jpg)

_Photo: Mount Kurikoma_

## **Tohoku Region**

### _Note:_

_1\. This article introduces the best time to view the foliage in each area’s onsen resorts, as well as a number of selected ryokans in each onsen area._

_2\. The best time to view fall colours listed here is based on open information published in Japan.（Survey date: November 14, 2025） Influenced by the weather and other natural factors, the actual period when autumnal leaf colouration meets its peak might be a little bit different from our prediction._

## **Oirase & Hakkoda Onsen**

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-01_Hakkoda-Ropeway.jpg)

### Hakkoda Mountains & Hakkoda Ropeway（八甲田山・八甲田ロープウェー）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=40.67578%2C140.85889&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early to late October

### Access

Three hours 10 min by JR Tohoku Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Shin-Aomori Station, then one hour by bus to Ropeway Station and right over there

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-02_Jogakura-Ohashi-Bridge.jpg)

### Jogakura Ohashi Bridge（城ケ倉大橋）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=40.65083%2C140.82601&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Mid to late October

### Access

(1) Approximately eight minutes by car from Ropeway Station

(2) One hour 10 min by bus from Shin-Aomori Station to Jogakura Onsen, then 20 minutes on foot

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-03_Oirase-Gorge.jpg)

### Oirase Gorge（奥入瀬渓流）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=40.52355%2C140.97389&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early November

### Access

(1) Approximately one hour 15 min by bus from Ropeway Station to Ishigedo, or

(2) two hours 20 min by bus from Shin-Aomori Station to Ishigedo, then right over there

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-04_Tsutanuma-Pond.jpg)

### Tsutanuma Pond, Tsuta Nana Numa (Tsuta Seven Lakes)（蔦沼・蔦七沼）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=40.60083%2C140.94996&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Late October

### Access

(1) Approximately 50 minutes by bus from Ropeway Station to Tsuta Onsen, or

(2) one hour 45 min by bus from Shin-Aomori Station to Tsuta Onsen, then 5 minutes on foot

[List of Ryokans in Oirase & Hakkoda Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/oirase-lake-towada-hakkoda-hot-spring)

## **Hirosaki Onsen**

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-05_Tsugaru-Iwaki-Skyline.jpg)

### Tsugaru Iwaki Skyline（津軽岩木スカイライン）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=40.64015%2C140.26162&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early to late October

### Access

(1) Three hours 10 min by JR Tohoku Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Shin-Aomori Station, then approximately one hour 30 min by car

(2) Approximately one hour by car from Aomori Airport

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2-07_Hirosaki-park.jpg)

### Hirosaki Park (Hirosaki Castle)＜弘前城（弘前公園）＞\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=40.6077%2C140.46436&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early to mid-November

### Access

45 minutes by JR Ou Main Line from Shin-Aomori Station to Hirosaki Station, then 15 minutes by bus to Shiyakusho-mae (City Hall) and 4-min walk from there

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2-10_shirakamisanchi.jpg)

### Lake Juniko & World Heritage Beech Forest Trail in Shirakami Sanchi Mountain Range（白神山地・十二湖・世界遺産の径ブナ散策道）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=40.56368%2C139.97969&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Late October to early November

### Access

(1) Three hours 10 min by JR Limited Express from Shin-Aomori Station to Juniko Station, then 15 minutes by bus to Oku-Juniko Lakes Parking Lot (Aoike Pond) and right over there

(2) Approximately two hours by car from Aomori Airport

(3) Approximately two hours by car from Akita Airport

(4) Approximately two hours by car from [Oga Peninsula Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/oga-hanto-hot-spring)

[List of Ryokans in Hirosaki Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/hirosaki-hot-spring)

## **Tsunagi-Oshuku Onsen**

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-09_Mt-Mitsuishi-Amihari-Lift.jpg)

### Mount Mitsuishi & Amihari Observation Lift（三ツ石山・網張展望リフト）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=39.82169%2C140.93638&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Late September to mid-October

### Access

(1) Two hours 10 min by JR Tohoku Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Morioka Station, 20 minutes by JR Tazawako Line from Morioka Station to Shizukuishi Station, then 45 minutes by bus to Amihari Onsen and right over there

(2) Approximately 30 minutes by car from Tsunagi-Oshuku Onsen

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-10_Hachimantai-Aspite-Line.jpg)

### Hachimantai Aspite Line（八幡平アスピーテライン）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=39.9548%2C140.88513&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early to mid-October

### Access

(1) Approximately one hour by car from Morioka Station

(2) Approximately one hour by car from Tsunagi-Oshuku Onsen

(3) Approximately one hour by car from [Yuze Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/yuze-hot-spring)

[List of Ryokans in Tsunagi-Oshuku Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/tsunagi-hot-spring)

## **Hanamaki Onsen**

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2-08_Chusonji-Temple02.jpg)

### Chusonji Temple, Hiraizumi（中尊寺・平泉）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=39.00173%2C141.10259&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early November

### Access

(1) Three hours 30 min by JR Tohoku Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Ichinoseki Station, or

(2) one hour by JR Tohoku Main Line from Hanamaki Kuko (Airport) Station (near Hanamaki Onsen) to Ichinoseki Station, then 25 minutes by bus to Chusonji

(3) Approximately one hour 15 min by car from [Minami Sanriku Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/minami-sanriku-hot-spring)

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-08_Chusonji-Temple.jpg)

### Motsuji Temple, Hiraizumi（毛越寺・平泉）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=38.9879%2C141.10786&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early November

### Access

(1) Three hours 30 min by JR Tohoku Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Ichinoseki Station, then 10 min by JR Tohoku Main Line to Hiraizumi Station and 7-min walk from there

(2) 50 minutes by JR Tohoku Main Line from Hanamaki Kuko (Airport) Station (near Hanamaki Onsen) to Hiraizumi Station, then 7 minutes on foot

(3) Approximately one hour 15 min by car from [Minami Sanriku Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/minami-sanriku-hot-spring)

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-17_Sukawa-Lake.jpg)

### Sukawa Highland & Sukawa Lake（須川高原・須川湖）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=38.97997%2C140.77037&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Mid to late October

### Access

One hour 30 min by bus from Ichinoseki Station to Sukawa Onsen, then right over there

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-18_Mt-Kurikoma.jpg)

### Mount Kurikoma（栗駒山）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=38.96084%2C140.78819&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Mid to late October

### Access

One hour 55 min by JR Tohoku Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Kurikoma Kogen Station, then approximately one hour 10 min by car to Iwakagami Daira

[List of Ryokans in Hanamaki Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/hanamaki-hot-spring)

## **Togatta & Kamasaki Onsen (Miyagi Zao)**

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-20_Zao-Echo-Line.jpg)

### Zao Echo Line（蔵王エコーライン）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=38.12215%2C140.44828&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early October to mid-November

### Access

(1) One hour 30 min by JR Tohoku Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Sendai Station, then approximately one hour 20 min by car

(2) Approximately 30 minutes by car from Togatta & Kamasaki Onsen (Miyagi Zao)

(3) Approximately one hour by car from [Zao Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/zao-hot-spring)

[List of Ryokans in Togatta & Kamasaki Onsen (Miyagi Zao)](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/togatta-kamasaki-miyagi-zao-shiroishi-hot-spring)

## **Minami Sanriku Onsen, Matsushima Onsen**

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2-41_matsushima.jpg)

### Matsushima Bay（松島）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=38.3673%2C141.05286&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early to late November

### Access

(1) One hour 30 min by JR Tohoku Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Sendai Station, then 40 minutesr by JR Senzan Line to Matsushima-Kaigan Station

(3) Approximately 50 minutes by car from [Akiu Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/akiu-hot-spring)

(4) Approximately one hour 30 min by car from [Zao Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/zao-hot-spring)

(5) Approximately two hours by car from [Ginzan Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/ginzan-hot-spring)

[List of Ryokans in Minami Sanriku Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/minami-sanriku-hot-spring)

[List of Ryokans in Matsushima Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/matsushima-hot-spring)

## **Akiu Onsen**

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-19_Akiu-Otaki-Falls.jpg)

### Akiu Otaki Falls（秋保大滝不動尊）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=38.27494%2C140.60385&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early to mid-November

### Access

One hour 30 min by JR Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Sendai Station, then 40 min by Akiu Kawasaki Sendai Seibu Liner to Akiu Sato Center (near Akiu Onsen) and 20-min taxi ride from there

[List of Ryokans in Akiu Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/akiu-hot-spring)

## **Kakunodate & Lake Tazawa Onsen, Yuze Onsen, Oga Peninsula Onsen**

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-15_Kakunodate-bukeyashiki.jpg)

### Kakunodate Samurai House（角館武家屋敷通り）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=39.59794%2C140.56216&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early to mid-November

### Access

(1) Three hours by JR Akita Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Kakunodate Station, then 15 minutes on foot

(2) Approximately two hours by car from [Yuze Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/yuze-hot-spring)

(3) Approximately two hours by car from [Oga Peninsula Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/oga-hanto-hot-spring)

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-16_Dakigaeri-Valley.jpg)

### Dakigaeri Valley（抱返り渓谷）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=39.6107%2C140.66421&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early November

### Access

(1) Approximately 15 minutes by taxi from Kakunodate Station

(2) Approximately two hours by car from [Yuze Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/yuze-hot-spring)

(3) Approximately two hours by car from [Oga Peninsula Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/oga-hanto-hot-spring)

[List of Ryokans in Kakunodate & Lake Tazawa Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/kakunodate-tazawako-hot-spring)

[List of Ryokans in Yuze Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/yuze-hot-spring)

[List of Ryokans in Oga Peninsula Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/oga-hanto-hot-spring)

## **Ginzan Onsen**

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2-40_ginzan-onsen.jpg)

### Ginzan Onsen（銀山温泉）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=38.57043%2C140.5303&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early November

### Access

(1) Three hours 50 min by JR Yamagata Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Oishida Station, then 40 minutes by bus to Ginzan Onsen

(2) 50 min by JR Ou Main Line from Yamagata Station ( [Zao Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/zao-hot-spring)) to Oishida Station, then 40 minutes by bus to [Ginzan Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/ginzan-hot-spring)

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-21_Naruko-Gorge.jpg)

### Naruko Gorge（鳴子峡）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=38.73283%2C140.69064&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Late October to early November

### Access

(1) Two hours 15 min by JR Tohoku Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Furukawa Station, 45 minutes by JR Rikuu East Line from Furukawa Station to Naruko Onsen Station, then 7 minutes by bus to Narukokyo Nakayamadaira Guchi and right over there

(2) Approximately 45 minutes by car from [Ginzan Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/ginzan-hot-spring)

(3) Approximately one hour 30 min by car from [Akiu Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/akiu-hot-spring)

(4) Approximately two hours by car from [Zao Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/zao-hot-spring)

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-24_Mogamigawa-River.jpg)

### Mogami Gorge & Mogamigawa River Cruise（最上峡・最上川舟下り）\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=38.4815%2C140.34653&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early November

### Access

(1) Two hours 50 min by JR Yamagata Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Yamagata Station, then 20 minutes by JR Rikuu West Line to Furukuchi Station and 5-min walk from there

(2) Approximately 50 minutes by car from [Ginzan Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/ginzan-hot-spring)

(3) Approximately one hour 40 min by car from [Zao Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/zao-hot-spring)

[List of Ryokans in Ginzan Onsen](https://selected-ryokan.com/ryokan/location/ginzan-hot-spring)

## **Tendo Onsen**

![](https://selected-ryokan.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2-25_Yamadera.jpg)

### Yamadera (Risshakuji Temple)＜山寺（宝珠山立石寺）＞\[ [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/1/edit?hl=ja&mid=1AaKCIR6el3L-w1iNkFUO5I-naa4iPWB6&ll=38.31311%2C140.4346&z=12) \]

### Best time to view fall foliage

Early to mid-November

### Access

(1) One hour 30 min by JR Tohoku Shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Sendai Station, then one hour by JR Senzan Line to Yamadera Station, or

web.description:
### Japan Fall Colors Forecast
The autumn foliage season for _momiji_ will likely begin in early October for Northern Japan, peaking around mid-November.
web.markdown:
[![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/kiyomizudera-temple-nighttime-illumination-fall-colors-kyoto-japan-1052-845x321.jpg)](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/kiyomizudera-temple-nighttime-illumination-fall-colors-kyoto-japan-1052-786x500.jpg "2025 Japan Fall Colors Forecast & Autumn Foliage Viewing Guide")

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/eikando-temple-kyoto-fall-colors-japan-150.jpg)

Our fall colors forecast for Japan offers peak viewing info & tips for popular autumn foliage spots, including Kyoto, Tokyo, Mount Fuji, Miyajima, Hiroshima, Himeji, and Nara. We’ll also share strategy for visiting the best temples, shrines, and evening illuminations.

Autumn is one of the most stunning times of the year in Japan, and one of the most popular times to visit. If fall colors season is your first time visiting Japan, you’ll likely be surprised by a couple of things: _crowds and colors_. On busy days and for evening illuminations, there will be lines to enter popular temples. At train stations and on buses, there will likewise be lines and extra crowd control to handle the influx of visitors.

There’s also a very good chance that these crowds will be heavier than normal. That has been the trend since Japan’s reopening, driven by a mixture of pent-up demand from domestic and international tourists. While the former should be close to exhausting itself, the latter is still an ongoing issue.

That’ll be especially true this year with the return of Chinese tour groups and potential for a weak yen inducing more demand among foreign visitors. That’s the bad news. (Well, partly bad–if you’re reading this English language site, a weak yen is probably positive news for you, even if it means more people!)

The good news is that it’s very much _worth it_. The vibrance of the fall colors throughout Japan (but especially Kyoto) is almost unbelievable. The resplendence of the Japanese maple trees and shades of crimson the leaves of these maple leaves take on is really something else. The abundant reds, yellows, and oranges juxtaposed against temples, shrines, and castles throughout Japan is stunning. It makes the otherwise unbearable crowds perfectly bearable.

We speak from experience. Fall colors season is our favorite time of year in Japan, surpassing even sakura. We’ve visited between October and December countless times–pretty much every year for the last decade-plus (minus 2020-2021 for obvious reasons), including several month-long stays. And we’ll once again be returning for another month-plus visit in November 2025.

During those extended visits, we made a concerted effort to find off the beaten path spots where fewer tourists ventured–we share those locations with you here. We’ve also learned how to make use of little-known resources put out by government agencies that offer forecasts and real-time updates on blooming progression.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/kyoto-fall-colors-calendar-real-time-progress.jpg)

Speaking of which, before we get going, we want to draw your attention to the City of Kyoto and Kyoto City Tourism Association [Fall Colors Calendar](https://kyoto.travel/en/autumnleaves/index.html) with all major temples, shrines, and other popular (and underrated) spots for foliage viewing. It’s not yet updated for 2025, but will be every Tuesday and Friday from mid-October through mid-December with the approximate progress of the color change.

We use this ourselves for both sakura and fall colors season, and it has proven both invaluable and accurate. It’s a great resource, and there’s really nothing else like it. We’ve tried other apps and sites, and none of them come close–presumably because none have the staffing or resources of the city itself. There’s also one by the [Central Japan Railway Company](https://souda-kyoto.jp/guide/season/koyo/) that’s pretty good, too. Anyway, we highly recommend bookmarking those pages for use right before or even during your visit.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/fall-colors-chureito-pagoda-mount-fuji-japan-728.jpg)

The other good news is that you can largely avoid the peak crowds and still see great color. This blog primarily focuses on Kyoto and Tokyo, and crowds peak in both locations around Labor Thanksgiving Day. We offer strategy for this in our [**Tips for Surviving Crowds in Kyoto, Japan**](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/avoid-crowds-tips-kyoto-japan/) and [**When to Visit Japan: Best & Worst Times**](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/when-visit-kyoto-japan-best-worst-times/) posts.

Due to Japan’s long north-south orientation, fall colors can be viewed somewhere in the country for three full months, with ‘peak colors’ spanning the entirety of October through December every single year. Fall colors start appearing in mid-September throughout the northern mountains of Hokkaido and Sapporo, and gradually spread to lower elevations and more southern areas, most notably Tokyo, followed by Kyoto & Osaka in late November and early December.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/kiyomizudera-temple-nighttime-illumination-fall-colors-kyoto-japan-1052.jpg)

### Japan Fall Colors Forecast

The Japan Meteorological Corporation has not yet released its first autumn foliage forecast for the 2025 fall colors season. The organization predicts the best time to see this year’s autumn leaves (momiji) and yellow leaves (gingko) for each city from Hokkaido to Kagoshima and about 700 autumn leaves spots throughout Japan.

Forecasts will be issued around the beginning of September, October and November 2025. As with other weather forecasts, these become increasingly accurate as fall foliage season draws nearer. The organization uses a proprietary prediction formula, developed based on past research, temperature trends, and other meteorological data to predict the peak leaf peeping seasons.

Please check back in early September 2025 for the first update on this year’s fall colors forecast for Japan. For now, here’s a look back at the first forecast from last September…

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/fall-colors-forecast-japan-november-december-2024.png)

The autumn foliage season for _momiji_ will likely begin in early October for Northern Japan, peaking around mid-November. At present, Sapporo’s predicted peak date is significantly later than normal.

Most cities throughout the Honshu mainland also have a delayed forecast, with their peaks coming only a few days later than normal. Late November or early December is the peak for Tokyo, Kyoto, and other popular tourist destinations. You could start the Golden Route tour in Tokyo the last week of November and likely hit the ideal colors in each destination along the way.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/fall-colors-forecast-japan-november-december-2024-2.png)

The forecast for yellow ginkgo leaves differs slightly than that for red maple koyo.

In Northern Japan, the best time is expected to be from early to late November. The mainland is expected to be in full bloom from mid-November to early December. That will extend to mid-month for some areas of western Japan.

Here’s this year’s fall colors forecast peak dates versus historical averages in major cities throughout Japan…

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Screenshot-2024-09-06-at-4.25.30-PM.png)

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Screenshot-2024-09-06-at-4.31.50-PM.png)

As you can see, Sapporo peaks earliest, with the best comes coming in October during a normal year. Of major tourist destinations, Tokyo and Nagoya follow that. Kyoto, Osaka, and the rest of the Kansai region sees the best colors in late November through mid-December.

Now let’s cover the best fall colors locations throughout Japan, starting in Kyoto…

### Kyoto’s Best Fall Colors Spots

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/eikando-temple-fall-colors-kyoto-japan-bricker-1201.jpg)

Kyoto gets its own section because it’s the epicenter of Japan’s fall colors season. If you’re visiting Japan during autumn to see the colors, Kyoto is _the_ essential city. Sure, there’s probably some remote mountainside that has quantifiably better autumn foliage, but Kyoto has what’s undeniably the best mix of natural and cultural beauty in Japan.

Rather than cobbling together your own fall colors itinerary for Kyoto, we’d recommend one of the following

- [**1-Day Kyoto Fall Colors Highlights Itinerary**](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/1-day-kyoto-japan-fall-colors-itinerary/)
- [**2-Day Kyoto Fall Colors Itinerary**](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/2-day-kyoto-japan-fall-colors-itinerary/)
- [**3-Day Kyoto Fall Colors Itinerary**](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/3-day-kyoto-japan-fall-colors-itinerary/)

If you have 4-5 days in Kyoto, add on our [**1-Day Kyoto, Kurama & Kibune Itinerary**](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/1-day-kurama-kibune-kyoto-japan-itinerary/) and/or our [**1-Day Nara, Japan Itinerary**](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/nara-japan-touring-plan/), both of which are general itineraries that are also optimized for autumn. We are not particularly keen on Osaka during fall colors season–the city can have pretty colors, but their not all that photogenic.

By contrast, in Kyoto dozens of the city’s best and most important temples are set ablaze in glorious shades of crimson, yellow, and orange between late October and mid-December. It’s an absolutely stunning scene that feels like you’re stepping foot into a painting.

We’ve visited over 100 temples & shrines in Kyoto during fall colors season, and these are our favorites…

[![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/bishamondo-temple-fall-colors-higashiyama-kyoto-japan-327x500.jpg)](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/bishamondo-temple-fall-colors-higashiyama-kyoto-japan.jpg)

**Bishamondo Temple** _–_ Located in Yamashina, a suburb of Kyoto, Bishamondo Temple is well worth the hike from Nanzenji Temple or the commute via train. The famous path of red Japanese maples that leads to the temple is the main draw here, but the inside of Bishamondo also is ablaze with fiery reds, punctuated by the occasional green.

Bishamondo is also beautiful and relatively serene, and draws fewer international tourists. We recommend Bishamondo if you have the time and can make it work with your itinerary, or want something a bit quieter.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/chionin-temple-autumn-fall-colors-sunburst-kyoto-japan-bricker.jpg)

**Chionin Temple**– Currently undergoing massive, multi-year construction ahead of the Tokyo Summer Olympics, Chionin Temple is a place about which I’m currently torn. On the one hand, it’s free and parts of it are stunning. On the other hand, construction spoils some of the atmosphere.

In terms of fall foliage, it’s not a must-do, but it’s still nice. If you do elect to visit Chionin Temple and venture to the back of its sprawling complex, you’ll be rewarded with some beautiful pockets of fall colors. There’s also an autumn nighttime illumination in the garden. Chionin Temple usually peaks around mid-November.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/eikando-temple-autumn-night-illumination-kyoto-japan-bricker.jpg)

**Eikando Temple** – This is one of Kyoto’s most popular temples during fall colors season. To see its entire area, you need to drop 1,600 yen (1,000 for a daytime visit and 600 at night). Visiting twice might seem redundant, but the entire temple is not open at night, and it’s a must-do in the autumn for both.

Even on a normal day, we feel Eikando is an underrated temple deserving of more attention. In November and December, it receives that attention, and for good reason is known as “Eikando of Fall Colors.”

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/enkoji-temple-northern-kyoto-japan-721.jpg)

**Enkoji Temple** – One of the most underrated temples in all of Kyoto, perched atop an overlook at the base of the mountains. Paths at Enkoji Temple will take you higher, giving you a breathtaking view above the tree line. Enkoji also has great range thanks to its numerous buildings, serene gardens, small bamboo forest, fusuma art, and more.

Although it’s listed earlier in the day in our fall colors itineraries, we favor visiting Enkoji Temple just before closing to watch/photograph the sunset over the fiery red trees. It’s the perfect way to end a day in Kyoto. Enkoji Temple tends to peak earlier due to its elevation.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/fall-colors-autumn-foliage-fushimi-inari-kyoto-japan-171.jpg)

**Fushimi Inari**– This is [our favorite shrine in Kyoto](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/fushimi-inari-kyoto-japan-review-tips/), and one you’ll seldom find listed as an autumn foliage location in Kyoto. This is sad and disappointing, as I found Fushimi Inari to be one of the better spots once you get up to the higher mountain loop.

The fact that the vast majority of visitors don’t get past the main loop probably explains why it’s not a recommended fall colors spot. However, if you’re willing to hike to the summit of Mt. Inari (and you absolutely should–it’s really not that bad of a hike), you’ll be rewarded with beautiful view, tranquility, and some vibrant color. I’d say this area of Fushimi Inari peaks in mid-to-late November.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/fall-colors-foliage-jojakkoji-temple-arashiyama-kyoto-japan-369.jpg)

**Jojakkoji Temple** – Within Arashiyama, there are several great fall colors spots: Iwatayama Monkey Park, Tenryuji Temple, Okochi Sanso Villa, and Nisonin Temple–just to name a few.

The standout of these is Jojakkoji Temple, which features a thick canopy of fall colors at the center of the temple, with a beautiful pagoda and sea of maple below as you climb higher along the hillside.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/fall-colors-garden-kitano-tenmangu-shrine-kyoto-japan-275.jpg)

**Kitano Tenmangu Shrine**– Often overlooked despite being only about a 20 minute walk from Golden Pavilion (which is _not_ a fall colors spot), Kitano Tenmangu Shrine is a great option for fall colors. Even if you linger at Golden Pavilion until it closes, you still should arrive here with enough time to experience sunset and the nighttime illumination in the Momiji-en (autumn maple garden) where you can see 350 maple trees.

While Kitano Tenmangu Shrine’s main areas are all free, they offer just a small scattering of autumn foliage as compared to the paid garden. We’d highly recommend doing that garden, and timing your visit to coincide with sunset and evening. Kitano Tenmangu Shrine tends to peak slightly later than the Kyoto average.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/kiyomizudera-fall-illumination-foliage-night-kyoto-japan-664.jpg)

**Kiyomizudera Temple**– Another [of our favorite temples in Japan](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/kiyomizudera-temple-kyoto-photos-tips/), we’ve frequently done Kiyomizudera’s nighttime illuminations, during both cherry blossom and fall colors seasons. The good news is that its iconic main hall is now completely uncovered, as the multi-year construction project has finished. This means _the_ iconic scene of Kiyomizudera is now possible again.

Despite this, it’s still one of the busier spots in Kyoto during the fall (or anytime, really). With both of those things in mind, we’d still strongly encourage you to visit: Kiyomizudera is worth it. Due to its number and variety of trees, I’d say Kiyomizudera Temple peaks slightly later and stays vibrant slightly longer than other temples in Kyoto. Anytime from the second week of November until the first week of December likely falls within the ‘peak’ time during a normal year.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/kodaiji-temple-autumn-night-illumination-kyoto-japan-bricker.jpg)

**Kodaiji Temple**– It’s really difficult to rank all of the autumn nighttime illuminations experiences we’ve had in Kyoto, but I’d be inclined to put Kodaiji Temple in the #1 slot. In large part, this is due to its diversity. There’s a placid reflecting pond lined with vibrant colors, beautiful rock and zen gardens, an illuminated bamboo grove…and a projection mapping show.

That last one might seem out of left field and is definitely not something you expect at a temple, but it’s surprisingly well-done. It makes good use of the environment and has some pretty visuals (AND DRAGONS!). The trees lining the hills at Kodaiji Temple are also stunning, making this a must-visit during the evening for any fall visitor to Kyoto. Kodaiji Temple has peak fall colors around mid-November.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/nanzenji-tenjuan-temple-kyoto-fall-colors-japan-151.jpg)

**Nanzenji Temple** – The good news about Nanzenji Temple ( [one of our favorite temples in Kyoto](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/nanzenji-temple-kyoto-tips-review/)) is that it has some of the best fall colors in Kyoto, much of the grounds where foliage is visible are free to explore, and it does a good job absorbing crowds.

The bad news is that Tenjuan Temple, the sub-temple where the autumn illumination occurs, is incredibly low capacity and draws lengthy lines even on weeknights. The foliage in Tenjuan Temple is beautiful and the lighting is careful, resulting in a wonderful experience–but the area is small. Nanzenji and Tenjuan Temples typically peak around late November.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/path-philosophers-kyoto-fall-colors-japan-152.jpg)

**Path of Philosophers** – Whereas the Path of Philosophers draws hordes of tourists during cherry blossom season (and rightfully so), it flies under the radar in the autumn. This is unfortunate.

[Path of Philosophers is a great walk any time of the year](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/philosophers-path-tips-kyoto-japan/)–plus it’s a good way to get between the various temples in this area–and it has patches of really vibrant reds and oranges, too. Path of Philosophers tends to peak slightly early, with vibrant colors in early to mid-November not being uncommon.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/fall-colors-shinnyodo-temple-higashiyama-kyoto-japan-324.jpg)

**Shinnyodo Temple** – This has all the makings of the type of temple we enjoy: free, tall pagoda, pretty, and did we mention _free_?! Despite being a short walk from Nanzenji, Shinnyodo is typically far less crowded.

Its fire-red and orange momiji maple and kaede maple, plus yellow ginkgo trees create such an oversaturated scene that almost looks surreal. Shinnyodo Temple is a definite sleeper pick for us, and we highly recommend it in the fall. This temple typically peaks in late November.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/shorein-temple-blue-lights-autumn-night-illumination-kyoto-japan-bricker.jpg)

**Shorein Temple**– The main draw during the autumn evening illuminations at Shorein Temple is the 1,000 blue lights that illuminate the ground outside of the main hall. There’s also lit-up foliage and a bamboo grove, among other things, but what draws most people here is the ground.

It’s a neat effect, to be sure, but I felt a tad underwhelmed seeing this in person. (Perhaps photos do it a bit too much justice?) It also seems to have less in the way of actual fall colors and more in terms of ‘warm lighting on normal trees.’ In any case, Shorein Temple is still a compelling evening option that draws fewer crowds than the high-profile temples. We recommend it mainly because other temples that do nighttime illuminations are a short walk from here, making it easy to visit.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/fall-colors-autumn-foliage-tofukuji-temple-tsutenkyo-bridge-kyoto-japan-164.jpg)

**Tofukuji Temple** – One of the most popular spots in autumn, Tofukuji is absolutely mobbed with people–a seemingly endless stream pouring off tour buses–throughout fall colors season. There’s a lot to see here, both free and paid. It’s also easily accessible via the train and from Fushimi Inari.

As such, it’s no surprise that Tofukuji enjoys such popularity, especially given the iconic Tsutenkyo Bridge and the colorful valley of trees. We’d recommend arriving as close to 8:30 a.m. as possible (advice we’ll be following ourselves when we revisit) to beat the crowds. _[Click here to see my fall colors photos of Tofukuji Temple, plus tips for visiting](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/fall-colors-tofukuji-temple/)._

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/yoshiminedera-temple-fall-colors-kyoto-japan-bricker-1200.jpg)

**Yoshiminedera Temple** – [In our full post about Yoshiminedera Temple](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/yoshiminedera-temple-review-info-tips/), we call it the southwestern version of Kiyomizudera or Kuramadera Temples. That’s high praise considering their quality, but Yoshiminedera is one of Kyoto’s crown jewels, which is also one of its best “hidden” gems.

As with any sprawling mountain temple in Kyoto, there are a lot of trees here and, consequently, a lot of pockets of color. Due to its elevation, Yoshiminedera Temple tends to be one of the first spots to change in Kyoto. It can be popular on weekends with Japanese visitors, but on weekdays it’s a pretty tranquil scene–you’ll seldom ever see a foreign tourist here.

### Our Favorite Fall Foliage Viewing Spots Elsewhere in Japan

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/hikone-castle-fall-colors-night-illumination-japan-2.jpg)

**Hikone**– This lakeside city can be visited as a day-trip from Kyoto, and is a smart option if the crowds are too heavy at Kyoto’s popular fall leaf viewing spots.

We recommend seeing Hikone Castle and Genkyuen Garden’s autumn illumination. This limited-time evening offering is beautiful and offered some incredibly photogenic scenes of Hikone’s peak autumn colors. _[Click here to see my autumn illumination photos from Hikone Castle & Genkyuen Garden](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/autumn-illumination-hikone-castle-genkyuen-garden/)._

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/himeji-castle-fall-colors-night-illumination-japan-dusk-bricker.jpg)

**Himeji**– While nothing can top Himeji Castle during cherry blossom season, autumn in the area is beautiful. Around the castle, trees are brilliant shades of red and yellow. Same goes for Kokoen Garden, which has its waterfalls framed by crimson maple trees making for a scene that is almost _too_ picture-perfect.

Engyoji Temple, the sprawling complex atop Mount Shosha, is an even better spot for fall colors in Himeji. These three spots form a perfect day-trip while in Kansai.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/hiroshima-a-bomb-dome-fall-colors-sunset-japan-bricker.jpg)

**Hiroshima**– Like Tokyo, Hiroshima is not typically viewed as a hotspot for fall colors.

However, there were pockets of beautiful trees (the one pictured above near the A-Bomb Dome was mesmerizing), especially around the Hiroshima Memorial Peace Park and along the water. It’s recommended if you’re more casual about seeing fall colors, and want to see them in an urban setting.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/miyajima-fall-colors-japan-149.jpg)

**Miyajima**– The island of Miyajima is about an hour train and ferry ride from Hiroshima, and is one of our favorite places in Japan. Miyajima normally has a long fall colors timeline due to the elevation differences between the peak of Mount Misen and the lower elevations literally on the water.

The areas around Miyajima’s many temples and shrines look other-worldly when bursting with color. For those planning a future fall colors tour of Japan, Miyajima is a must-visit in our estimation.

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/mount-fuji-fall-colors-autumn-foliage-japan-190.jpg)

**Mount Fuji –** Whether you’re heading to Fuji Five Lakes or Hakone, you won’t be disappointed with Mount Fuji in the autumn. Hakone is the more popular of the two, and where most tourists to Japan head due to ease.

We prefer the Lake Kawaguchiko area, which includes the famed Maple Corridor, Chureito Pagoda, and shoreline autumn illumination at Lake Yamanaka.

[![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/kasuga-taisha-shrine-deer-fall-colors-nara-japan-772-343x500.jpg)](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/kasuga-taisha-shrine-deer-fall-colors-nara-japan-772.jpg)

**Nara** – Pretty much the entirety of Nara is a treasure trove of fall colors beauty. Our [1-Day Nara, Japan Itinerary](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/nara-japan-touring-plan/) offers the perfect approach, and makes it easy to accomplish if you’re doing a day trip from Kyoto or Osaka.

In our experience, colors peak in Nara slightly before they do in Kyoto, and inexplicably linger for quite a while. Even after the leaves have fallen, it’s still a beautiful scene, as they form a beautiful blanket of color for the [Devious Deer of Nara, Japan](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/deer-nara-japan/).

![](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/shinjuku-gyoen-national-garden-tokyo-japan-121.jpg)

**Tokyo**– As Japan’s largest city and tourist destination, Tokyo is obviously a popular spot for fall colors viewing. Unfortunately, the urban environment doesn’t really lend itself to this.

You’ll want to seek our public parks and gardens if you’re looking for the best views of autumn foliage. Shinjuku Gyoen is the most popular spot; get there early to beat the crowds. We also like Rikugien Garden, which is great but quieter and more intimate.

That covers everything…for now. Despite visiting literally hundreds of fall colors locations throughout Japan, there are still spots we haven’t seen. This includes the Alpine Route, Daisetsuzan National Park, Nikko, Mount Hakkoda, and other mountainous hikes. Our goal is to continue exploring Japan’s beautiful fall colors spots, updating this as we go.

**If you’re planning a trip to Japan that includes Kyoto, we recommend that you start by consulting our [Ultimate Guide to Kyoto, Japan](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/kyoto-japan-planning-guide/) to plan all aspects of our vacation. You should also check out [our other posts about Japan](https://www.travelcaffeine.com/location/japan/) for ideas on other places to visit!**

## Japan Autumn Foliage Forecast 2026

Although Japan’s fall color forecast varies from year to year, it’s not quite as temperamental as the one for cherry blossoms. As a result, even if a warmer autumn leads to an later season or a cooler one leads to an earlier one, I’ve founded that most years are pretty similar.

When is autumn in Japan 2026? Well, the Japan Meteorological Corporation will release its first forecast in early September 2026, which will predict how peak color will be compared to a “normal” year. However, do keep in mind that forecasts aren’t generally accurate until much later in the season—take the first one with a grain of salt.

Regardless of a particular forecast, here are the approximate times you can expect to enjoy autumn colors in Japan:

| Destination | Yellow leaves | Red leaves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Daisetsuzan** | September 15 | September 25 |
| **Hachimantai** | October 5 | October 15 |
| **Mt. Hakkoda** | October 15 | October 25 |
| **Kakunodate** | October 25 | November 5 |
| **Nikko** | October 25 | November 5 |
| **Koyasan** | October 25 | November 5 |
| **Kurobe Gorge** | November 5 | November 15 |
| **Tokyo** | November 25 | December 5 |
| **Takayama** | November 5 | November 15 |
| **Fuji Five Lakes** | October 25 | November 5 |
| **Kanazawa** | November 15 | November 25 |
| **Kyoto** | November 25 | November 25 |
| **Setouchi** | November 25 | November 25 |
| **Shikoku** | November 25 | December 5 |
| **San’in** | November 25 | November 25 |
| **Kyushu** | November 25 | December 5 |

As far as how I formulate my autumn color forecasts, in 2026 and otherwise? If the months of September and October are warmer than average, I expect autumn colors to appear later than usual. The inverse is also true: In colder years, autumn colors come to Japan sooner. Other factors can also delay the colors or bring them forward, mostly notably rainfall (or lack thereof)

In order to monitor this for yourself, keep an eye on temperatures in the cities or prefectures where you want to enjoy fall foliage, and compare them to the averages you find posted online. You can also check “Recent” pictures of your target destinations on Instagram, although you should make sure they were recently taken, and not just recently posted.

## Best Places to See Autumn Leaves in Japan in 2026

### Kyoto

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Daigo-ji.jpg)

As is the case during the spring with the _sakura_, Kyoto is one of the most satisfying places in Japan to see autumn colors, no matter what the [Kyoto autumn](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/09/13/where-can-you-see-fall-colors-in-kyoto/) leaves forecast 2026 ends up holding. My favorite places in Kyoto to see autumn colors include **Arashiyama** ( **Tenryu-ji** temple, **Okochi Sanso Villa** and the entire shoreline of the **Katsuura River**) as well as **Higashiyama** temples like **Nanzen-ji** and **Kiyomizu-dera**, and more distant temples such as **Daigo-ji** and **Kurama-dera**. There are also many awesome [Kyoto autumn color](https://japanstartshere.com/2018/12/03/autumn-in-kyoto/) spots on the periphery of the city, from **Tofuku-ji** along the **Nara Line** en route to **Fushimi** district, to **Kurama-dera** north of the center.

### Tokyo

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Tokyo-Autumn.jpg)

Now, I’d like to tell you where you can go in Tokyo to enjoy autumn for yourself, whether for Tokyo autumn 2026 or another year. Obviously, the most famous [autumn color spot in Tokyo](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/12/12/see-autumn-leaves-in-tokyo/) is **Meiji Jingu Gaien**, aka **Ginkgo Avenue**, but that’s not the only game in town. In particular, I love **Koishikawa Koraku-en** and **Rikugi-en** gardens within the city limits; **Yokohama**‘s **Sankei-en** garden is also very worth a visit, if you have time during your fall 2026 Japan trip. Additionally, as you can see above, colorful trees (especially yellow ginkgos) are strewn throughout the heart of the city, including in **Marunouchi** just west of **Tokyo Station**.

_NOTE: Tokyo is obviously also a great base for day trips to Japan autumn destinations, including **[Hakone](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/22/hakone-in-autumn/)** and **Kamakura**. **Nikko**, too, although that one deserves its own section, which you will find below._

### Mt. Fuji

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Mt-Fuji-Autumn.jpg)

The autumn forecast Japan 2026 can be vague for areas around [**Mt. Fuji**](https://japanstartshere.com/mt-fuji-travel-guide/), since they differ so much in terms of elevation and other climactic conditions. For instance, while it’s possible to see autumn colors in coastal **Shizuoka** prefecture and even along the shores of **Lake Kawaguchi** and **Lake Yamanaka** well into the end of November, you’ll want to visit earlier in the month (or maybe even October) if hiking trails closer to Japan’s most famous mountain are [where you want to see Fuji’s autumn colors](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/19/mt-fuji-in-autumn/). Early November, meanwhile, is usually the best time to get the “money shot” behind **Chureito Pagoda** in **Fujiyoshida**.

### Hokuriku

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Eihei-ji-Autumn.jpg)

Irrespective of whether you plan to visit during autumn Japan 2026 or another year, **[Hokuriku](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/22/hokuriku-in-autumn/)** is one of my favorite places in Japan to enjoy autumn colors. The obvious choice here is **[Kanazawa](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/05/07/things-to-do-in-kanazawa/)** and its famed **Kenroku-en** garden, though I wouldn’t sleep on neighboring areas, be that **Nata-dera** temple in **Komatsu** (which, like Kanazawa, is in **Ishikawa**), or Eihei-ji temple in **Fukui** or **Kurobe Gorge** in **Toyama**. As a general rule, colors further from the sea and higher in elevation will change first, with red leaves reaching their peak as early as the first week of November and as late as the first week of December.

### The Japanese Alps

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Takayama-Autumn.jpg)

Whether in Fukui, Kanazawa or Toyama, Hokuriku is just a stone’s throw from the **[Japanese Alps](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/19/japanese-alps-in-autumn/)**, which are bounded by Nagano on the other side. If you’re coming to this region during the month of October, you might want to visit the **Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route** near **Toyama** or **Kamikochi Valley** near **Matsumoto**. In November, on the other hand, autumn colors along the historical [**Nakasendo Trail**](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/11/30/nakasendo-trail-guide/) will be nearing their peak, as will those in **Shirakawago** and **Takayama**. You could also visit the somewhat understated **Monet’s Pond** in **Gifu** prefecture, though in this case I recommend going in the very early morning to avoid crowds

### Koyasan

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Koyasan-Autumn.jpeg)

**Wakayama** prefecture’s **[Mt. Koya](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/02/21/koyasan-temple-stay/)** is a somewhat evergreen destination (and not just because of all the evergreen trees atop it), but especially shines in the autumn, when [colors usually peak in early-to-mid November](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/19/koyasan-in-autumn/). While colors are at their most dramatic at the **Danjo Garan** sacred complex and in **Koyasan Town**, there are a surprising number of red maples and yellow ginkgoes in **Okuno-in** cemetery, in spite of it being typically defined by its iconic cedar trees.

### Nikko

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/Nikko-Autumn.jpg)

I can understand why **Nikko**, a histor city in **Tochigi** prefecture just north of Tokyo, might seem like an afterthought for your Japan autumn 2026 trip. Most people come to this place, which centers around 17th-century **Tosho-gu** shrine as a day trip from Tokyo, assuming they come at all. This is complicated in autumn, at least if you’re not careful: While Tokyo’s leaves tend to change around or just before December 1, Nikko’s (particularly those near **Kegon Falls** and **Lake Chuzenji**) often turn yellow, orange and red a full month (or even six weeks!) earlier.

### Hokkaido

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Hokkaido-Blue-Pond.jpeg)

Another place to go if you’ll only have time to visit Japan during the earlier part of the season? **[Hokkaido](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/10/31/hokkaido-autumn-itinerary/)** [autumn](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/10/31/hokkaido-autumn-itinerary/) 2026 may be your best bet for seeing leaves! For visits in early-to-mid October you’ll want to head east from **Sapporo**, whether to the **[Shirogane Blue Pond](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/10/31/how-to-visit-shirogane-blue-pond/)** in **Biei** near **Asahikawa**, or even over to **Sounkyo Onsen** or up to **Mt. Daisetsuzan**.

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Hakodate-Autumn.jpg)

Or to the wild **Shiretoko Peninsula**, be it to the inland lakes of **Kussharo**, **Mashu** and **Akan**, or past the town of **Utoro** toward the **Shiretoko Five Lakes** marsh. If you’re visiting in late October or early November, meanwhile, this is when Sapporo-adjacent autumn spots such as the _onsen_ towns of **Jozankei** and **Noboribetsu** will see their colors change; underrated **[Hakodate](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/02/17/things-to-do-in-hakodate/)** will also peak at this time.

### Tohoku

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Lake-Towada-Autumn-1.jpg)

Japan’s superlative **[Tohoku](https://japanstartshere.com/tohoku-travel-guide/)** region, meanwhile, sees leaves change a bit later than Hokkaido—which is to say, in line with when many places in North America and Europe experience autumn. If you’re planning an October or early November autumn trip to Japan, therefore, it makes sense to visit the northern half-dozen prefectures of Honshu island.

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Kakunodate-6.jpg)

Some of my personal favorite spots in these regions for autumn colors include **[Lake Towada](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/29/lake-towada/)** and **Oirase Stream**, both in **[Aomori](https://japanstartshere.com/aomori-travel-guide/)** prefecture, as well as **[Yamadera](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/12/08/yamadera-day-trip/)** temple in **Yamagata** and **Ouchi-juku** village in **[Fukushima](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/11/30/is-fukushima-worth-visiting/)**. I also love the autumn colors in **[Kakunodate](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/10/05/is-kakunodate-worth-visiting/)** _Samurai_ village, at **Geibikei** gorge and in **[Hiraizumi](https://japanstartshere.com/2024/05/06/is-hiraizumi-worth-visiting/)**, aka the “Kyoto of the North.”

### Setouchi

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Bitchu-Matsuyama-Castle-1.jpg)

I feel like the **Seto Inland Sea** is not among the top destinations people search when consulting the Japan autumn leaves forecast 2026. But it should be. Foliage in **[Setouchi](https://japanstartshere.com/setouchi-travel-guide/)** is magnificent even in the major cities of the region: In **[Hiroshima](https://japanstartshere.com/hiroshima-travel-guide/)** near the **A-Bomb Dome**; at **Okayama**‘s **Korakuen** garden; and in **Ritsurin**, **Takamatsu**‘s treasure. Obviously, this beauty is even more pronounced the more off the beaten path you go, be that to **Bitchu Matsuyama**‘s “castle in the clouds,” to deer-filled **[Miyajima](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/12/08/is-miyajima-worth-visiting/)** island or to the harbor city of **[Onomichi](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/12/05/is-onomichi-worth-visiting/)**, whose **Old Temple Trail** is arguably at its most enchanting during the autumn.

### San’in

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/Sanin-Japan.jpg)

Heading to the other coast of far-western Honshu island takes up to **[San’in](https://japanstartshere.com/2024/04/10/sanin-itinerary/)**, which is in general one of my favorite regions of Japan. Autumn colors here are pretty “late” in general, usually peaking around early December in the castle city of **[Matsue](https://japanstartshere.com/2024/12/25/is-matsue-worth-visiting/)**, at **[Izumo Shrine](https://japanstartshere.com/2024/12/25/how-to-visit-izumo-shrine/)** and in underrated Yonago, though certain destinations (towering **Mt. Daisen**; inland **[Nageirei-do](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/03/06/nageiredo-temple-hike/)** temple) can see their colors peak in November. No matter when you come, however, you’re guaranteed a relatively tranquil and tourist-free _momijigari_ experience.

### Iya Valley

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Iya-Valley-Autumn.jpg)

I briefly mentioned **[Shikoku](https://japanstartshere.com/shikoku-travel-guide/)** autumn colors earlier in the context of the **Seto Inland Sea**, but I wanted to call particular attention to those in the inland **[Iya Valley](https://japanstartshere.com/2023/08/27/iya-valley-itinerary/)**. There are a couple of advantages to going here, and not just because of how much the wild scenery suits the blazing leaves of fall in Japan. For starters, whether at **Oboke Gorge** or near the **Kazurabashi Vine Bridge**, peak season here tends to be in mid-to-late November, several weeks earlier than in Shikoku’s cities. This can make an excursion here worthwhile even if you can’t stay into December, which is when most leaves in southern Japan are at their most brilliant.

## When Does Japan’s Autumn Foliage Usually Peak?

Whether we’re talking about autumn foliage Japan 2026 or in general, autumn leaves in Japan follow a rather predictable pattern. Specifically, you can expect to see peak _koyo_ color according to the following calendar:

- **Late September:** Hokkaido and high-altitude [Tohoku autumn](https://japanstartshere.com/2025/12/19/tohoku-in-autumn/) destinations
- **Early-to-Mid October:** Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route; Tohoku’s Aomori prefecture
- **Late October to Early November:** The rest of Tohoku; the [Japanese Alps](https://japanstartshere.com/japanese-alps-itinerary/); Fuji Five Lakes; [Nikko](https://japanstartshere.com/2022/11/23/how-many-days-in-nikko/); [Mt. Koya](https://japanstartshere.com/2018/06/11/koyasan-temple-stay/)
- **Mid-to-Late November:** [Kanazawa](https://japanstartshere.com/kanazawa-travel-guide/); [Kansai](https://japanstartshere.com/kyoto-osaka-itinerary/); Setouchi; most of Shikoku; most of [Kyushu](https://japanstartshere.com/kyushu-travel-guide/); [San’in](https://japanstartshere.com/japan-off-the-beaten-path/)
- **Early December:** [Tokyo](https://japanstartshere.com/places-to-visit-in-tokyo/) and southern Kyushu, plus [Shikoku](https://japanstartshere.com/shikoku-travel-guide/)

You should note that these dates represent the peak of colors for all trees, whether for autumn in Japan 2026 or a different year. Japanese authorities also release a so-called “yellow leaves” forecast, which predicts when Japan’s famous ginkgo trees will change colors.

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Shirakawago-Autumn.jpg)

## Is it Too Early to Plan a Japan Autumn Itinerary?

Autumn in Japan 2026 will start when the hillsides of Daisetsuzan National Park blaze red and orange in late September or early October. Accommodation for major Japan autumn leaves destinations will quickly fill up for 2026, so I’d recommend booking your hotels and ryokan as soon as possible.

Have your flights and hotels booked, but need help stringing it all together? You can [hire me to plan the ultimate Japan itinerary!](https://japanstartshere.com/japan-itinerary/)

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Japan-Autumn-Photography.jpg)

## Other FAQ About Autumn in Japan 2026

### What months are autumn in Japan 2026?

Japan’s autumn colors begin in Hokkaido in late September, color the hillsides of Tohoku and the Japanese Alps from mid-October through mid-November, and reach their peak in Kyoto, Hiroshima and eventually Tokyo as November gives way to December.

### Where should I go in Japan in autumn?

As I mentioned in the beginning of this article, you can find autumn beauty throughout Japan, from rural hillsides and gorges in Hokkaido and the Tohoku regions, to ancient historical districts from Kyoto’s Higashiyama ward to the town of Takayama in the Japanese Alps.

### Is it cold in autumn in Japan?

Japan can be downright hot at the official beginning of autumn in late September, with temperatures in major cities well above 25ºC or 80ºF. However, by the times leaves change wherever you choose to see them, things will have cooled down substantially. You can expect crisp days with temperatures around 10ºC, and chilly nights approaching (or sometimes dipping below) freezing.

![](https://japanstartshere.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Japan-Autumn-Night.jpg)

## The Bottom Line

Whether it’s six months or just six weeks away by the time you read this, autumn in Japan 2026 is closer than you think—the time to start planning is now! Split a week or two in late November between Tokyo and Kyoto, or come earlier in the season and visit somewhere more non-traditional, be that in off-the-beaten path Tohoku or in the scenic Fuji Five Lakes region. One thing to note about Japan fall foliage 2026, if you’re feeling stressed, is that they’re much less fickle than the [cherry blossoms](https://japanstartshere.com/cherry-blossom-season-japan/)—they last longer, too. Still, if you’re feeling uneasy about planning your trip or simply don’t have time to do it, there’s another option. web.markdown:

The Japan Meteorological Corporation has released its second fall foliage forecast, predicting that autumn colors in Tokyo will reach their peak around December 1.

![Foilage 2025](https://cdn.japan-forward.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Foilage-2025-1024x576.jpg)

If cherry blossoms define Japanese spring, then colorful foliage is the highlight of autumn. Warmer-than-usual temperatures are expected across Japan through October 2025, which may cause the fall colors to appear on time or slightly later than average this year.

## **A Delayed Foliage Season**

### **Northern Japan**

Includes: Sapporo, Hakodate, Lake Towada, Sendai

Peak viewing:

- Mountains: Early October to mid-November
- Lowlands: Late October to late November


Expect foliage to emerge around the usual time or slightly later. Cooler weather in November should bring vivid reds and golds.

### **Eastern Japan**

Includes: Tokyo, Nikko, Nagano

Peak viewing:

- Mountains: Late October to early December
- Lowlands: Late November to mid-December

### **Western Japan**

Includes: Kyoto, Osaka, Hiroshima, Fukuoka

Peak viewing:

- Mountains: Early November to early December
- Lowlands: Late November to mid-December


In Kyoto and Nara, vibrant maple leaves should shine from late November to early December, with golden ginkgo trees peaking around the same time.

## **Expected Foliage Dates by City**

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| **City** | **Expected Peak Foliage Date** |
| Sapporo | November 9 |
| Sendai | November 27 |
| Tokyo | December 1 |
| Kyoto | December 12 |
| Osaka | December 5 |
| Fukuoka | December 9 |

A late foliage season gives travelers plenty of time to plan their trips. The following are some popular destinations to enjoy fall colors.

[![Japan 2 Earth Masthead Banner](https://cdn.japan-forward.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/japan-2-earth-masthead-v2.jpg)](https://featured.japan-forward.com/japan2earth/)

## **1\. Iwate: Esashi-Fujiwara Heritage Park**

This 20-hectare theme park recreates Japan's Heian Period (794–1185), including aristocratic residences and ancient fortresses. The wooden replica of Kyara no Gosho, home of the Oshu Fujiwara clan, is especially picturesque in fall, with maple trees reflected in the pond.

Fall illuminations begin on October 17 on select dates. The entrance fee is ¥1,000 ($7) for adults.

![](https://cdn.japan-forward.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/X2LOCX55LNPF3DTT7WCB4UMHWQ-1024x507.jpg)_Fall illumination at the Esashi Fujiwara Heritage Park on October 27, 2023. (©Sankei by Yukihiro Ishida)_

## **2\. Miyagi: Naruko Gorge**

A 100-meter-deep gorge carved by the Otani River, Naruko Gorge transforms into a vivid patchwork of reds, yellows, and oranges. The Ofukazawa Walking Trail from Naruko Gorge Resthouse to Otani River offers stunning views, including the iconic Ofukasawa Bridge.

![](https://cdn.japan-forward.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/2ZRY22ORTBIRTPRM5FD262RN6U-1024x684.jpg)_Naruko Gorge, one of the top fall foliage spots in Miyagi Prefecture on October 30, 2023. (©Sankei by Akimitsu Kikuchi)_

[![Japan 2 Earth Masthead Banner](https://cdn.japan-forward.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/japan-2-earth-masthead-v2.jpg)](https://featured.japan-forward.com/japan2earth/)

## **3\. Aomori: Nakano Momiji Mountain**

Known as the "Little Arashiyama of Tohoku," this mountain has been a fall favorite since the Edo period. Tsugaru Yasuchika, the 9th lord of Hirosaki, once imported about 100 maple varieties from Kyoto.

The combination of foliage, waterfalls, and the Nakano River creates a spectacular panorama. The "kanpu-dai" viewing platform is just a 10-minute walk up the mountain.

![](https://cdn.japan-forward.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/DMKXH7MOQFMI5ID2B3RBZC45BE-681x1024.jpg)_Nakano Momiji Mountain in Aomori Prefecture at the peak of fall foliage on October 30, 2023. (©Sankei by Noriyuki Fukuda)_

## **4\. Fukushima: Mount Ryozen**

Rising 825 meters (2,707 feet), Mount Ryozen is famous for its dramatic rocky surfaces, which turn yellow and red in autumn. Designated a national Place of Scenic Beauty, the mountain offers challenging hiking trails with ladders and chains. Views from the summit are breathtaking, attracting around 40,000 visitors each season.

![](https://cdn.japan-forward.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/U26R62YGR5I67O2BHG7EUPTMDM-1024x647.jpg)_Mount Ryozen in Fukushima Prefecture during the fall. (©Sankei by Nobuo Serizawa)_

[![Japan 2 Earth Masthead Banner](https://cdn.japan-forward.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/japan-2-earth-masthead-v2.jpg)](https://featured.japan-forward.com/japan2earth/)

## **5\. Tochigi: Shiobara Onsen Village**

This hot spring village in Nasushiobara City boasts 60 hotels and 150 springs. Historically enjoyed by the Utsunomiya clan and later by Crown Prince Yoshihito (future Emperor), Shiobara combines relaxing onsen with beautiful autumn scenery.

![](https://cdn.japan-forward.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/JEMMTRCNURLNDMWXOKEGVOQJOY-1024x683.jpg)_Sightseers enjoy the foliage in Nasushiobara City, Tochigi Prefecture. (©Sankei by Toshiyuki Izawa)_

## **6\. Shizuoka: Shuzenji Onsen**

One of the oldest hot spring towns on the Izu Peninsula, Shuzenji has been popular with literary figures like Ryunosuke Akutagawa and Natsume Soseki. Shuzenji Nature Park has around 1,000 maple trees, while nearby Niji no Sato offers illuminated nighttime foliage displays.

![](https://cdn.japan-forward.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/SU2WKWDAHFIFJILKFXZSHI54FA-1024x681.jpg)_Foliage light-up event at Shuzenji Niji-no-Sato in Izu City, Shizuoka Prefecture. (Courtesy of the Izu City Industrial Promotion Council)_

## **7\. Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Rout** e

Spanning the Northern Alps between Toyama and Nagano, this scenic route reaches Mount Tate at 3,015 meters (9,890 feet). The full route is open until November 30, showcasing foliage at different altitudes, with views accessible by bus, cable car, and walking trails, offering a diverse and unforgettable autumn experience.

![](https://cdn.japan-forward.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/MOET2YC4CRK6TMQA7ZAYGPTZXI-1024x655.jpg)_Autumn foliage around the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route in Tateyama, Toyama Prefecture on October 13, 2023. (©Kyodo)_

_The predictions are based on the_ [_Japan Weather Corporation's forecast_](https://n-kishou.com/corp/news-contents/autumn/?lang=en "") _._
